title: Resilient streaming: connection handoff, context propagation, and cancellation safety in Go SDK
creator: Priya Singh
body:
Summary:
We need to improve the Go SDK streaming implementation to make connection handoffs (reconnects, transparent failover) and context cancellation robust and ergonomically simple for application developers. Current issues observed during early adopter testing: lost partial responses when client context is canceled during in-flight buffering, confusing error semantics when the transport dies during a graceful shutdown, and leak-prone goroutine handoffs when retrying/resuming a session.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Documented, easy-to-use client pattern for: graceful shutdown, immediate cancel, and resumable handoff where supported by the server.
- No goroutine leaks in common cancellation + reconnect scenarios (unit/integration tests must assert goroutine counts).
- Predictable error types: Cancelled vs DeadlineExceeded vs TransportError vs ResumeUnavailable.
- Example code for producers showing correct usage of Contexts and cancellation windows.
- Backwards-compatible public API change (minimal surface).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
1) Two cancellation layers: caller-level Context and internal stream lifecycle context. The public APIs accept a Context; internally we keep a short-lived streamCtx per connection to bound I/O. On handoff we carefully propagate caller cancellation but avoid interpreting internal timeouts as caller cancellations. This reduces surprising Cancel semantics but adds complexity to shutdown code.

2) Prefetch buffer semantics: we will keep a small in-memory prefetch queue for streaming messages (size controlled by config). If a caller cancels while messages are buffered, we will return buffered messages first if the developer used the provided StreamReader helper (explicit Drain on cancel). Otherwise we will return a Cancelled error and provide a method to retrieve buffered fragments for advanced use (advanced API, opt-in). Trade-off: returning buffered messages on cancel may mask cancellation intent; we mitigate by requiring explicit Drain() or a boolean flag on stream creation.

3) Handoff / Resume: server-side resume tokens are supported in protocol; client will attempt a single transparent reconnect + resume when transient transport error is detected. If resume fails, client falls back to a terminal error and surface ResumeUnavailable. This keeps optimistic resume but avoids indefinite retries.

API surface proposal (high level):
- Stream(ctx, opts...) -> (StreamHandle, error)
- StreamHandle.Next(ctx) -> (Message, error)  // respects caller ctx and returns well-defined errors
- StreamHandle.Drain(ctx) -> ([]Message, error) // drain buffered messages during cancel/shutdown
- StreamHandle.Resume() -> (bool, error) // explicit resume attempt for advanced scenarios
- Config: PrefetchSize, ResumeEnabled, ResumeRetryPolicy, InternalIOTimeout

Implementation notes:
- Introduce stream lifecycle manager that owns 3 goroutines: recv loop, buffer manager, and lifecycle supervisor. The supervisor serializes handoff: it pauses delivery, swaps transport, replays resume handshake, and unpauses delivery. All pauses are cooperative and bounded by InternalIOTimeout to avoid stalling app contexts.
- Use context.Value to tag correlative IDs for observability across handoff.
- Avoid canceling the caller-provided ctx from within the SDK. Instead return contextualized errors which embed original cancellation cause.
- Add a strict Close() vs Cancel() distinction: Close waits for Drain (bounded) then closes; Cancel aborts immediately and returns Cancelled error.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for error mapping, buffer drain semantics, and supervisor state transitions.
- Integration tests that simulate: mid-message transport drop, immediate caller cancel, slow Drain under backpressure, and successful resume. Use deterministic fake transports to simulate race conditions.
- Load test on staging to validate no goroutine leaks under 1k concurrent streaming clients for 30m.

Examples / Developer guidance (to include in docs):
1) Graceful shutdown pattern:
   ctx, stop := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
   defer stop()
   sh, _ := client.Stream(ctx, client.StreamOptions{PrefetchSize: 8})
   go func() {
       for {
           m, err := sh.Next(ctx)
           if err != nil {
               if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
                   // application requested cancel; drain if desired
                   msgs, _ := sh.Drain(context.Background())
                   handleBuffered(msgs)
                   return
               }
               log.Error("stream error", err)
               return
           }
           handle(m)
       }
   }()

2) Immediate cancel semantics example (no drain):
   ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 50*time.Millisecond)
   defer cancel()
   sh, _ := client.Stream(ctx, client.StreamOptions{PrefetchSize: 2})
   m, err := sh.Next(ctx) // will return context.DeadlineExceeded if not ready

Migration notes:
- Public API kept mostly compatible. We add StreamOptions and new helpers but maintain existing Stream(ctx) overload. Default behavior preserves previous semantics (no auto-drain on cancel).

Open questions / risks:
- How should SDK surface partial messages that arrive during cancel? (we propose Drain opt-in).
- Resume replay costs for large KV caches — on resume we might need to rehydrate small routing state; requires server-side limits. Need coordination with runtime team.
- Observability: add per-stream metrics for handoff attempts, resume success/failure, drain counts. Impacts console dashboards.

Progress / work log:
- 2026-02-12: spike completed exploring supervisor pattern; prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/tree/stream-supervisor-spike
- 2026-02-20: design review with runtime team — agreed on single transparent resume attempt then fail. Action: runtime to expose "resume_token" TTL header (ENG-642100).
- 2026-02-28: implemented supervisor + buffer manager in feature branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/2531 (WIP).
- 2026-03-05: integration tests added for transport drop case, but observed goroutine leak in path where resume fails while caller canceled. Root cause: supervisor waiting for Drain on canceled context.
- 2026-03-08: addressed leak by making supervisor use a bounded internal context (InternalIOTimeout) for lifecycle ops; PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/2547
- 2026-03-12: smoke tests pass locally; preparing for internal review.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/streaming-handoff-design (internal)
- Observability proposal: https://docs.redwood.ai/obs/stream-handoff-metrics (draft)

Next steps / TODOs:
- Finish API docs and examples for code samples and add to README (owner: Diana Wu).
- Run full staging load test (owner: Ethan Cole) and validate goroutine stability and metric emission.
- Add documentation section to Console release notes describing new stream metrics and how to interpret resume failures.
- Cut go-sdk-1.9.0-beta for early access customers and gather feedback on drain ergonomics.

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the semantic distinction between Close() vs Cancel() and whether Drain should be default for Close(). I recommend Close() performs a bounded drain while Cancel() aborts immediately.
- Runtime team dependency: ensure resume_token TTL is present and documented in protocol.
